html:
SMTO-RST-0002 — This task's history belongs to a different conversation

GUID: dee540ee-7e34-4278-9a19-5d1eead71680
Slug: run-journal-scope-mismatch
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't save or continue this task because its saved history is tied to another conversation. SMTO won't move a task's history between conversations, so nothing was moved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation where this task first ran, and check its latest results to see what it already did. SMTO stopped this step, so the results show how far the earlier work actually got.
  2. Continue or resume the task in that same conversation. Each task's history stays with the conversation that started it.
  3. To use that work somewhere else, send a new message in the other conversation describing the results you need. A new message starts its own history instead of borrowing one from another conversation.

What success looks like

  • The task continues in its original conversation, or the new message runs without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the names of both conversations, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't copy or move SMTO's saved files between conversations by hand.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Run/journal binding found the run bound to a different conversation in native_run_journals, or a save without an expected journal head would replace a retained transcript prefix.

What this means

  • Run/journal binding finds conflicting conversation ownership, or a save without an expected head attempts to replace a retained transcript prefix. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Run/journal binding finds conflicting conversation ownership, or a save without an expected head attempts to replace a retained transcript prefix.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare run ID, bound conversation/journal and exact retained transcript prefix.

How to fix it

  • resolve_native_journal_id or MemoryRunStore._bind found a conflicting conversation_id for the run's journal binding, or the supplied history does not match its journal prefix. Resume the run from its bound conversation, or start a new run or continuation; inspect current state and existing receipts first, and do not rebind journals or substitute run identities across conversations.
  • Select the owning conversation and its original saved run. Do not move journals or substitute execution identities across conversations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported operations preserve one coherent conversation-owned journal without moving identities across scopes.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
